articleTitle: A Method of Defect Characterization in Guided Wave Testing Using Persistent Homology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Guided wave based non-destructive testing technique has been widely used in many engineering structures. Accurate characterization of defects by extracting defect-related features from the guided wave testing signals is very important for the condition evaluation of the tested specimen. In this paper, a topological feature for defect characterization is extracted from the topological domain of the guided wave testing signal. Specifically, the topological feature is extracted from the 2-dimensional phase space of the testing signal based on persistent homology. The steel wire notch experiments show that there is an exponential relationship between the topological feature and the cross sectional area loss ratio of the steel wire, and the goodness of fit is 0.9962. This paper confirmed that the persistent homology is a useful tool to analyze guided wave testing signals to investigate the defect characterization.

articleTitle: Ultrasound-guided wave dispersion curve reconstruction based on generalized dispersive mode decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In non-destructive testing, the received signal may be a multi-mode overlapped guided wave. To extract effective properties of the waveguide, appropriate signal processing methods must be used to separate the individual modes. In this paper, a semi-analytical finite element method is first used to establish a theoretical model for the propagation of Lamb waves in a plate, and the theoretical dispersion curve is calculated based on this model. Then, the Generalized dispersive mode decomposition method is used to separate Lamb wave signals with multiple modes overlapped, and separate $\boldsymbol{A}_{\mathbf{0}}$ and $\boldsymbol{S}_{\mathbf{0}}$ modes can be obtained. Subsequently, the reconstructed dispersion curves corresponding to the separated $\boldsymbol{A}_{\mathbf{0}}$ and $\boldsymbol{S}_{\mathbf{0}}$ modes can be obtained by executing the zero-crossing technique. Finally, by comparing the reconstructed results with the theoretical dispersion curve, the effectiveness of the Generalized dispersive mode decomposition method in Lamb wave mode separation is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Nondestructive inspection of subsurface defects in metals by transient lock-in thermography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, transient lock-in (TLI) thermography is used as a non-destructive inspection technique to detect the subsurface defects in metals. Initially, the transient thermal response is obtained by removing the dc term from the raw LI thermal image sequences using pixel-wise polynomial fits. And then, the phase and amplitude images at the excitation frequency are extracted from the transient thermal response by the discrete Fourier transformation. Meanwhile, two metals specimens, including aluminum alloy and Q235 steel, with different sizes and depths of artificial flat-bottom holes (FBHs) are also used to demonstrate the performance of the TLI thermography. Finally, a quantitative comparative analysis based on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and runtime is conducted to show the superiority of the TLI modality to detect the subsurface defects in metals.

articleTitle: The Wavenumber-domain Algorithm in Multi-mode Imaging for Full Matrix Capture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ultrasonic imaging with full matrix capture (FMC) data is an emerging technique applied for nondestructive testing (NDT) of various industrial components. Nevertheless, this imaging modality suffers from heavy burden of reconstruction time consumption due to the large size of FMC data. Recently, wavenumber-domain reconstruction of ultrasonic imaging like extended phase shift migration (EPSM) taking advantages of computational efficiency have been developed to replace conventional time-domain reconstruction methods, especially for light-weight real-time NDT. However, current EPSM can only support direct-mode ultrasonic imaging, and multi-mode, like half-skip and full-skip modes, ultrasonic imaging can detect cracks near bottom boundary that is insensitive to direct-mode. To this end, EPSM is extended to adapt for multi-mode ultrasonic imaging, including half-skip, full-skip and wave mode conversion cases in this paper. The performance of the proposed reconstruction method is demonstrated by experiments, and the results shows the proposed method achieves equivalent imaging quality but with up to one-sixteenth time consumption compared with conventional time-domain reconstruction.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic defect detection of railway wheels based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ultrasonic testing is a highly efficient NDT technique, which is widely used and rapidly developing among the many NDT methods. With the rapid development of high-speed railways, existing testing speeds are often unable to meet demand. Wheel integrity is essential for safety. Existing ultrasonic testing techniques now rely more on the intuition and experience of skilled workers, which often results in a high rate of missed inspections. In this paper, images of wheels with different defect depths are firstly annotated and calibrated. Secondly, the structure of the YOLO v5 algorithm is improved for the characteristics of ultrasonic defects, making it more efficient for recognizing B-scan defect images of wheels. Finally, the data is validated and tested for each category. The experimental results show that the improved algorithm has significantly enhanced the performance of wheel B-scan defect recognition, reducing the false alarm rate while stabilizing the detection speed of one wheel within 10s.

articleTitle: A Sound Velocity Calibration-Based Ultrasonic Total Focusing Method Imaging of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced polymers (CFRP) have been widely used in various industries such as aerospace and automotive due to their remarkable mechanical properties. However, the inherent anisotropy of CFRP leads to significant variations in sound velocity along different directions, which greatly affects the quality of ultrasonic total focusing method (TFM) imaging. To address this challenge, this study proposes a TFM imaging technique based on sound velocity calibration. First, the sound velocity curves at different angles were obtained using the backwall reflection method (BRM). Then, the TFM imaging technique was calibrated using the angular sound velocity curves. The effectiveness of the proposed method was experimentally validated on both unidirectional and multilayer CFRP specimens. The results show that the choice of inspection direction affects the angular sound velocity curve, and selecting an appropriate inspection direction can effectively improve the accuracy and image quality of TFM imaging.

articleTitle: Dual-student Feature Fusion Knowledge Distillation Model for Wheel Tread Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The defect of the wheel tread is an important factor affecting the normal work of railway train wheels. Traditional deep learning object detection algorithms require a large number of samples to train models, and their detection performance is limited by the type and quantities of abnormal samples. Faced with the lack of ab-normal samples of wheel tread defects, this paper proposes to use an unsupervised knowledge distillation anomaly detection model to complete the task of anomaly detection on wheel treads. In order to reduce the influence of the non-tread area on the anomaly detection model, the tread area is segmented by Unet, and then a dual-student feature fusion network is designed to improve the reconstruction ability of the student decoder for normal features in the reverse knowledge distillation structure. In training, the two student networks jointly learn the knowledge of normal features from the teacher network, cooperatively memorize the features of normal samples, and play the advantage of fusion features in reasoning to strengthen the reconstruction of normal features by the student network. Experiments show that the improved model can achieve 92.3% AUC, 85.3% precision, 95.3% recall and 88.0% accuracy on the railway wheel tread dataset. Compared to the unimproved model, the model detection performance is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Research on Defect Evaluation Method of Aluminum Plate Based on Frequency-Sweep SH Guided Wave
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a new defect evaluation method of aluminum plate based on frequency-sweep Shear Horizontal (SH) guided wave is proposed. First, a finite element model for the SH guided wave in aluminum plate is established. Slot defects and through-hole defects are simulated and analyzed. The defect types could be identified according to the shape of the reflection coefficient versus frequency curve. The reflection coefficient of slot defect can be used to quantify random defects by quadratic fitting curve with the defect depth. The minimum value point of the reflection coefficient curve for through holes can be used to quantify the diameter of through-hole, which is 0.42 times of wavelength of the SH guided wave. Then, the feasibility of the evaluation method is verified experimentally. The quantitative error for slot defects does not exceed 10.0%, and the quantitative error for through-hole defects hardly exceeds 5.0%.

articleTitle: Detection System Using Flexible Differential Eddy Current Sensor for Non-destructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: High pressure hydrogen cylinder is an important equipment for hydrogen storage and transportation. Regular nondestructive testing of aluminum liner microcracks of hydrogen cylinder is necessary to ensure the safe use of high-pressure hydrogen cylinder. Due to the small volume and narrow mouth of the hydrogen storage bottle, the traditional detection methods are difficult to implement, so a detection system suitable for the detection of the inner surface of hydrogen cylinders is urgently needed. In this paper, a flexible differential eddy current sensor is designed based on the principle of eddy current testing. The feasibility of the sensor is verified by establishing a finite element model, and the influence of various parameters on the sensor response is analyzed. A scanning system suitable for the detection of the aluminum liner of hydrogen gas cylinders is designed. The scanning system can enter the interior of the aluminum liner of the hydrogen cylinder, and is equipped with an eddy current sensor to fit the inner surface of the aluminum liner for detection. The experimental results show that the sensor can suppress the common mode component in the signal, and has a high signal to noise ratio. What is more, the scanning system can complete the rapid scanning of the hydrogen cylinder liner, which verifies the feasibility of the detection system.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation about Effects of Stress on Different Cumulative Second Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves technology has shown excellent application potential in the field of structural stress testing due to its unique nonlinear characteristics and long distance detection range. However, the diversity and complexity of effects about stress on different cumulative second harmonics constrain the development of related research. In this paper, a numerical study about the response Law of different cumulative second harmonics with stress is undertaken based on ABAQUS software. A plate finite element model is established and the corresponding simulation experiment is carried out. The simulation result demonstrates that the variation tendencies of different cumulative second harmonic modes with stress are different, and their relative nonlinear parameters are monotonically increasing or decreasing with the increase of tensile stress. Therefore, in the application of stress detection, it is essential to analyze the response law of the selected cumulative second harmonic mode with stress change in advance. The simulation method proposed in this paper is also applicable to other studies about nonlinear ultrasonic waves and has wide applicability.

articleTitle: Finite element simulation of ultrasonic reflection characteristics in layer-dropping composite structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to study the ultrasonic propagation characteristics in the layer-dropping structure, this paper obtained the elastic matrix parameters of carbon fiber reinforced composite lay-up at any ply angle by introducing the concept of elastic matrix rotation transformation on the basis of analyzing the characteristics of the layer-dropping structure. The finite element method was used to perform numerical simulation and visualize the ultrasonic propagation process. With the non-reflective boundary condition set, the ultrasonic propagation characteristics of different upper and lower surface angles and heights in the layer-dropping structure are simulated. The simulation results show that when the angle is greater than 60° with the depth of the layer-dropping structure area is 12mm, the ultrasonic signal incident perpendicular to the upper surface cannot be reflected back to the upper surface through the lower surface. In this case, defects close to the bottom surface cannot be detected using ultrasonic reflection method.

articleTitle: A ID SAFE/SAFE mode-matching approach for Lamb wave scattering study in bent plates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: A one-dimensional(1D) mode-matching approach to handle Lamb wave scattering in bent plate is proposed in this article. The eigenvalue problem associated with guided waves along circumferential direction of the curved plate is constructed in Comsol using semi-analytical finite element(SAFE) method, and together with that in flat plate are solved in frequency-domain. In both cases the mode solutions corresponding to all real and a number of complex wavenumbers with the least imaginary parts, are used to one-dimensional field-matching at the junctions of them to get the scattering matrix of Lamb modes. In comparison with the time or frequency domain two-dimensional numerical models, theoretically with less calculation cost and modeling complexity, the method manifests almost equal effectiveness and mutual verification from experiments. It’s found among all the coefficients, the mode transmitting in themselves usually dominate the scattering energy, except the cases when the bent have a rigid inner corner, a 180° bent angle, or the incident waves are at the cut-on frequency of propagating mode.

articleTitle: Control of Residual Stress and Deformation of Aluminium Triplet Cylinder by Power Ultrosound Beam
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of poor dimensional accuracy of components and low production efficiency caused by residual stress in the machining process of triplet cylinder, a method of using high-energy ultrasound to adjust and control the residual stress of components was proposed, so as to control the deformation of components and improve production efficiency. By measuring the residual stress distribution state of components at different stages, verify the reduction effect of high energy ultrasound on the mechanical residual stress of components, and finally analyze and count the key dimensions of components controlled by high energy ultrasound to determine the feasibility and reliability of this method for actual production. The results show that high energy ultrasound can effectively reduce the original stress of the blank and the residual stress caused by the processing stage, and finally obtain the components with fully qualified dimensional accuracy. This method plays an important role in the efficient production of this type of triplet cylinder.

articleTitle: A Domain-adaptive Method of Binocular Disparity Estimation for Bottom Components of the Train
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Disparity estimation of binocular images is an important branch of depth reconstruction. The neural network method based on depth learning shows excellent performance in binocular stereo vision, which is far beyond the traditional binocular depth estimation algorithm. Most binocular stereo matching networks rely on training the dataset of the target scene, and can not predict the disparity of bottom components of the train directly. For this problem, we propose a domain-adaptive network, which includes two types of feature extraction encoding layers, a cost volume module that fuses a pair of image features, and a disparity prediction module based on multi-scale convolution layer. Moreover, based on the results of network prediction, we use a consistency checking method to further refine the disparity and enhance the reliability of the estimation results. Through experiments in different scenes, our method shows more accuracy and generalization than ordinary stereo matching networks, and has good effect of stereo visualization with less memory consumption in real train scenes. At the same time, our optimization method of consistency reduces the error of prediction and improves the confidence of disparity estimation for train bottom as a whole.

articleTitle: Fast Imaging Method of Total Focusing Method in Nozzle Weld Inspection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The development of phased array ultrasonic testing (PAUT) using the total focusing method (TFM) has led to improved quality in the detection and characterization of defects that may occur in device components. The transducer is usually coupled to the specimen via the plexiglass wedge to allow for the transfer of energy into target areas when using PAUT with full matrix capture (FMC). Due to the vast number of transmission delay sequences and the calculation power necessary to receive the focus for ultrasonic inspection using PAUT with FMC, a time-efficient technique for finding the incidence point is critical. This paper describes a segmental search method (SSM) for quickly determining the point of incidence of a wedge dual-layer medium. The search interval was narrowed by imposing the constraint that the point of incidence should be between the source and the target. In addition, finding the appropriate step size for the search range minimized the time spent on search processing. This method can be computationally more efficient than the analytical method (ANM) and Newton iteration method (NIM) used to solve Snell’s law and can ensure beam accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Pulsed Eddy Current Testing Technology for Cladding Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Compared with traditional eddy current flaw detection, pulsed eddy current has wider frequency bandwidth and stronger penetration ability, which is often used in the detection of cladding pipes. To solve the disadvantages of low detection sensitivity and large volume of existing eddy current probes, a small probe design is proposed, which can detect surface defects under large lift-off distance. Finite element simulation and experimental tests are used to compare and analyze the influencing factors and effects of the pulsed eddy current testing. A three-dimensional finite element model is established to study the pulsed eddy current distribution and detection voltage form of the proposed probe on the specimen. Through the pulsed eddy current experiment, the detection voltage decay curve was obtained, and the peak voltage was quantitatively fitted. The experimental results show that the detection probe can effectively detect the surface square hole defect under 10mm lift-off distance. Moreover, the defect depth can be identified through the peak voltage change. The defect detection voltage curve is obtained through the defect scanning experiment, which is consistent with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Application of cylindrical phase shift migration algorithm with vector coherence factor(CPSM-VCF) on Ultrasonic Imaging Detection of Bearing ring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Precision bearings are key transmission components of high-speed machine tools, trains and industrial robots, which always under high load and high-speed work condition. Internal cracks can easily cause the fracture failure of the bearings. Therefore, this paper proposes a cylindrical phase shift migration (CPSM) algorithm combined with vector coherence factor(VCF) for ultrasonic imaging detection of bearing rings. First, raw ultrasonic data is acquired by scanning along a circumference direction of a cylinder. The phase of the ultrasonic data is calculated through the Hilbert transform and Euler formula. The sine and cosine value matrixes of the phase are performed to construct the VCF. Then, the CPSM image reconstructed from original ultrasonic field is weighted by VCF. Finally, the image reconstructed by CPSM-VCF method is obtained. To verify the effectiveness of the above method, water immersion ultrasonic testing experiment of cylindrical specimen and rolled bearing ring was carried out. The results show that the signal-noise ratio (SNR) and lateral angular resolution of the reconstructed image were improved by CPSM-VCF. This research provides an efficient and low-cost ultrasonic imaging algorithm to detect rolled bearing rings.

articleTitle: A fast finite element modeling and solving method for 2D defect magnetic leakage field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper a two-dimensional fast finite element model is proposed, which can shorten the calculation time while ensuring the accuracy. Through the theoretical derivation of the finite element numerical calculation, the finite element model of the leakage magnetic field is established. First, the six-node triangular element is used to divide the grid, then the sparse matrix is used to solve the equations, and then the magnetic potential is solved by using the orthogonal basis of the zero space of the boundary condition matrix. The performance of the model is significantly improved.

articleTitle: Effect of Green function model for the ultrasonic time reversal based super resolution imaging algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of Green function model on the ultrasonic time reversal (TR) based super resolution (SR) imaging algorithm has been investigated. Time reversal with multiple signal classification (TR-MUSIC) and phase-coherent multiple signal classification (PC-MUSIC) have been introduced as the typical TR based SR imaging algorithms. Point spread function modelling has been implemented to compare the performance of TR-MUSIC and PC-MUSIC when different Green function models were applied in the imaging process. An experimental ultrasonic array imaging system has been built to capture the real ultrasonic array data from the steel sample with a EDM line, which can be considered as the extended target. It is shown that PC-MUSIC is sensitive to the Green function model when compared with TR-MUSIC. When proper Green function model is chosen, the shape of extended target in solid can be distinguished and its size can be evaluated based on PC-MUSIC image.

articleTitle: Study of Multi-parameters Separation for Oxide Film Thickness Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The zirconium cladding is one of the most important safety barriers of a nuclear power plant. An oxide film may be formed on the outer surface of the cladding during the usage in the nuclear reactor, which seriously affects the safety and performance of the fuel assembly. How to measure the oxide film thickness with high-precision is still a problem to be studied. This paper proposes an oxide film thickness measurement method based on frequency-sweeping eddy current testing, which suppresses the effects of the interfering parameters by fusing the multi-frequency measurements. The influences of the excitation frequency, conductivity of the cladding tube and metal coating thickness on the oxide film measurement are analyzed. Then the algorithm of accurately calculation of the oxide film thickness is derived and verified. The results show that the calculation error of the oxide film thickness is less than 1 micron with different cladding conductivities.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Infrared and Visual Fusion Detection Framework for Near-Surface Defect in Moving Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Traditional infrared thermal testing (IRT) is susceptible to surface conditions such as variation of surface emissivity, which may lead to false detection and has high requirements for the flatness and cleanliness of the sample. Traditional visual testing (VT) could capture surface texture information with high resolution but lacks the ability to detect sub-surface defects. This paper proposes a multispectral fusion detection framework in moving mode combines the advantages of IRT and VT for real-time detection and classification of both surface defects and sub-surface defects. The designed multispectral fusion detection system can adjust the trajectory and speed for different materials and shapes of specimens and collect time-synchronized infrared and visible image pairs for further processing. The proposed algorithmic framework enables real-time end-to-end fusion detection by fast coarse registration and late fusion. Comparative experiments have been conducted on four standard and natural samples of different materials and shapes to validate the reliability and efficiency of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Testing of Fatigue Cracks in Aluminum Alloy Based on Orthogonal Matching Pursuit and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The fatigue cracks in aluminum alloy are difficult to identify by ultrasonic testing (UT) due to insufficient signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) induced by the narrow crack gaps and the close acoustic impedances between defects and material. In this paper, the combination of orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed to improve the SNR of ultrasonic signals. The matching process of OMP is optimized by using the PSO with a global search to find the best atoms for weakening noise, reconstructing signals and recognizing defects. The experimental results indicate that the root-mean-square error (RMSE) and smoothness r are effectively reduced by this method for the array signals with noise from the fatigue crack with 3 mm height in aluminum alloy. Finally, we compared the processing effects of OMP without and with PSO. The efficiency is enhanced more than 11 times with a stable denoising effect by introducing PSO.
